title: Build exact full-sector memory with finite rotor and mechanical kinetic energy
statement: For H_eta=H_G+E_R(N-1/2-eta)^2-lambda Y(2cos phi), J=e^(i phi)R_phi and C=P_m e^(i pi N) satisfy [H_0,J]=0,[H_eta,C]=0,CJC^-1=-J and JH_etaJ=H_-eta. All eta=0 sectors pair. The complete infinite ladder has bounded actual kinetic energy at fixed parameters; a fixed sufficient regime E_R>=128K*, E_R/(k_B T0)>=10 yields <Q>_+>1/2 and opposite dipoles <Y>_+>lambda/(2k0).

requires: Complete periodic half-charge rotor with fixed E_R, bounded Q=2cos(phi), centered positive Gaussian support and actual Ycos(phi) force; eta=0 for exact J conservation and pairing. Uniform spring/temperature/cutoff limits as in the proof.
provides: For H_eta=H_G+E_R(N-1/2-eta)^2-lambda Y(2cos phi), J=e^(i phi)R_phi and C=P_m e^(i pi N) satisfy [H_0,J]=0,[H_eta,C]=0,CJC^-1=-J and JH_etaJ=H_-eta. All eta=0 sectors pair. The complete infinite ladder has bounded actual kinetic energy at fixed parameters; a fixed sufficient regime E_R>=128K*, E_R/(k_B T0)>=10 yields <Q>_+>1/2 and opposite dipoles <Y>_+>lambda/(2k0).
assumptions: The normal ladder remains; adjacent-level Q matrix elements are nonzero. Detuning is unbounded on the ladder and no uniform relative transition bound is supplied. Cosine bias breaks C; sine defects generally break J. No rotor cold-heat law or acquired control precision follows.
costs: Fixed sufficient E_R may be large but need not grow as T falls. Pay the actual rotor kinetic bound, half-offset/symmetry precision, source/control/field-generator and preparation/readout interfaces.
contract.units: N,eta,J eigenvalues and Q are dimensionless; E_R is energy, lambda QY energy, C compliance, dipole Y length. All kinetic bounds use actual minimally coupled angular momentum.
contract.obstruction: A protected sector and finite energy remove the free-doublet/hidden-inertance objection but do not establish the required eta-dependent heat response.

body: Half-offset gauge makes rotor functions antiperiodic; J sectors fold to opposite ND/DN intervals, leaving an infinite normal coordinate rather than a two-state truncation. Symmetric charge cutoffs preserve J and bounded Q, and the confining rotor kinetic/form/trace limit extends the finite-force theorem. A half-spring square inequality and convex log partitions bound the actual rotor kinetic energy. An excited-projector penalty with exact E_R/4 cancellation bounds normal excitation; bounded Q and force balance then give the full-sector dipole. Conserved J gives static autocorrelation weight by the conserved-charge bound, not heat scattering.
